news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

news_drafts.headline: SWestrans faces losing £525k in active travel grants
news_drafts.lead: The South West of Scotland Transport Partnership (SWestrans) is forecast to lose £525,000 in government funding for active travel projects because the money will not be spent in time and cannot be carried forward. The partnership's revised budget for Transport Scotland's Active Travel Infrastructure Fund is £1.7 million, but only £682,000 is forecast to be spent by the end of the financial year. Transport Scotland's ring-fenced annual funding does not automatically carry forward; the £525,000 shortfall in its Tier 1 allocation will be permanently lost. A further £554,995 of the revised budget remains unallocated to individual projects. Officers are developing allocation proposals for the next Board meeting, with schemes needing to be committed by 31 December 2026 and spent by 31 March 2027.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway Council faces £74 million funding gap despite 15 years of cuts
news_drafts.lead: Dumfries and Galloway Council faces a projected funding gap of £74 million over five years, despite having already cut £137 million from its budget since 2011. The council's financial strategy shows annual shortfalls starting at £11.87 million in 2027/28 and rising to £15.50 million by 2031/32, with limited room for further cuts to protect services. Public sector pay rises of £8–9 million annually must be absorbed within existing budgets, while costs to repay borrowing for capital projects will peak at £2.1 million in 2028/29. Audit Scotland warned in January that Scottish councils are increasingly reliant on temporary fixes to balance their books and have depleted reserves—leaving less room for emergency spending.

findings.paper_title: 07.10.26 HSC Harbours Capital and Revenue Final Report
findings.headline: Council has secured £58,668 in external Coastal Benefit Fund grants for harbor improvements.
findings.detail: The council has successfully applied for and received funding from the Coastal Benefit Fund for improvements at two harbours: £23,617 for Isle of Whithorn (quayside resurfacing, work complete) and £35,051.40 for Garlieston (quay pathway and storage enhancements, due to start October 2026). This external funding reduces the burden on the council's own capital resources.
findings.matters: This demonstrates the council can secure external funding for harbor assets and provides offset to the infrastructure investment required.
findings.figures: Isle of Whithorn: £23,617 (complete); Garlieston: £35,051.40 (starts Oct 2026); total £58,668.40
findings.quote: £23,617.00 has been awarded to Isle of Whithorn harbour for quayside resurfacing and line marking. This work is complete. £35,051.40 has been awarded to Garlieston harbour for enhancements to the quay pathway and storage area.

findings.paper_title: 07.10.26 HSC Harbours Capital and Revenue Final Report
findings.headline: Stranraer Marina construction will reduce annual revenue by £17-20k for approximately two years, requiring support from other budget areas.
findings.detail: When construction begins, three of five pontoons will be removed for about two years, causing significant revenue loss that cannot be covered by the harbours budget alone. The council will need to fund this loss from other parts of the Economy and Infrastructure budget. Estimated annual income loss is £17,223.52 to £19,658.56 depending on whether commercial vessel discounts are maintained.
findings.matters: This represents a material addition to the council's budget pressures during the project period and indicates cross-service budget pressure at a critical time.
findings.figures: Estimated annual revenue loss: £17,223.52 (Option 2) or £19,658.56 (Option 1); construction period approximately 2 years; current annual marina income £97,192.20
findings.quote: This income loss cannot be covered by harbours revenue budget and will have to be cover by funding from other areas of the Economy and Infrastructure budget.

findings.paper_title: 07.10.26 HSC Harbours Capital and Revenue Final Report
findings.headline: Harbours service requires ongoing council subsidy with revenue variance of £75,049 against budget.
findings.detail: The service has a structural operating deficit where revenue income falls short of expenditure by significant amounts, requiring the council to allocate funds to cover the gap. For 2026/27, the budget variance is -£75,049 with an allocated revenue budget of £94,414. This pattern is consistent, with 2025/26 showing a variance of -£58,094 and 2024/25 a variance of -£135,673.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether this service can become self-sustaining and what the ongoing trajectory of council subsidy is.
findings.figures: 2026/27 budget variance -£75,049; allocated revenue budget £94,414; 2025/26 variance -£58,094; 2024/25 variance -£135,673
findings.quote: The Harbours allocated revenue budget for 2025/26 is £94,414. This is the sum required to supplement expected income to cover the total Harbour service revenue expenditure.

findings.headline: Social care audit action implementation delayed by Health and Social Care Partnership restructuring; framework nearing completion
findings.detail: Implementation of audit recommendations for Assessed Care Needs has been slower than anticipated due to significant organisational change within the Health and Social Care Partnership, including a restructure realigning social work and social care services under a single Social Work Manager. A Quality Assurance Framework is nearing completion and revised timescales for remaining actions will be confirmed once the framework is finalised and new management arrangements are embedded.
findings.matters: Delayed implementation of control improvements in social care—a typically high-spend service area—extends a control assurance gap during a period of organisational change.
findings.quote: Management have advised that progress against the audit actions has been impacted by a period of significant organisational change within the Health and Social Care Partnership (HSCP), including a restructure which has realigned social work and social care services under a single Social Work Manager.

findings.headline: Council has secured over £50m in Levelling Up Fund government grants and is delivering multi-project capital programme on schedule
findings.detail: Dumfries and Galloway has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund, with £17.7 million allocated to the Reactivating Galloway Project. Capital projects are delivering on track: Stranraer Watersports Hub construction began February 2025 with opening due September 2026; Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels is nearing completion; the George building, which initially lacked a clear use, now has 8 expressions of interest and a tender exercise in progress.
findings.matters: Securing and successfully delivering a £50m+ government capital programme strengthens the council's asset base, improves its financial position, and demonstrates project delivery capability.
findings.figures: over £50 million received; £17.7 million for Reactivating Galloway Project
findings.quote: The Council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling up Fund of which £17.7 million was for the Reactivating Galloway Project.
